Parliament
National Assembly
Proceedings of the Twenty-First Session
Full Details of Proceedings
Ashoj 2083
4th Monday
Meeting Number - 48
Presided over by the Chairperson, the meeting commenced at 13:23 hrs.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, today's meeting of the National Assembly begins at 13:23 hrs. Honorable members, names have been submitted to speak during the Zero Hour. I will now provide time to speak. First, Honorable Member Meena Singh Rakhala.
Honorable Member Meena Singh Rakhala (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Honorable Chairperson, today the prices of every daily essential commodity in the market have increased. Gas is not easily available. Even essential goods are suffering from inflation. The biggest impact of this is on the poor, laborers, low-income families, and citizens who live on daily wages. Festivals are also approaching. The general public is worried about whether to celebrate the festival with their families or to gather expenses for survival. The government's attention does not reach the people, not even to the kitchen. I draw attention to making daily essential goods available to the public at affordable prices and controlling black marketing, artificial scarcity, and price hikes. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Ram Kumari Jhankri.
Honorable Member Ram Kumari Jhankri (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Honorable Chairperson, I have been seeing daily incidents of EV vehicles catching fire. For this reason, I want to draw the government's attention that we have freely imported EV vehicles for trade deficit, fuel consumption, or our commitment to zero-carbon aviation. However, there was no state policy regarding their standards, criteria, and what to do with the batteries after their lifespan. As a result, a more dangerous situation is about to arise regarding their hazardous waste. Therefore, whatever vehicles have been imported and have come into the market, what are their standards, what is their quality, what is the process of checking them, what is their capacity, what are the safety standards? What are the national and international safety standards? No policy has guided our EV vehicles in these matters. Therefore, I want to draw the government's attention that it is necessary to bring a clear policy and law for EV vehicles. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Rekha Kumari Jha.
Honorable Member Rekha Kumari Jha (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Honorable Chairperson, the incident of beating and mistreatment of a journalist from Rautahat at the Nepal-India border crossing of Bairgania has been publicized. I demand an impartial investigation into the incident and action against the culprits. I want to ask the government directly whether those who attack journalists have no fear of the law, or if the state's security mechanism is weak? If a journalist writes a wrong news, there is a legal way to refute it. But no one has the right to assault a journalist over the content of the news. Madhesh should not be turned into a smuggling hub. The border should not be allowed to become a safe passage for criminals. The situation where information is made public and security is ensured cannot be more unacceptable. Providing security to journalists is not just about providing security to individuals; it is about protecting the public's right to information and democracy. Therefore, I urge the government to immediately address the issue of criminals... (Time expired).
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Roshni Mechhe.
Honorable Member Roshni Mechhe (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Honorable Chairperson, bilateral talks between ministers of two nations are very important regarding diplomatic dignity, interests, and relations. Certain basic sensitivities must be maintained during talks. The fundamental principles of diplomatic language are respect, reciprocity, and transparency. Ministerial bilateral meetings should also be seen as opportunities for agreement, management, and trust-building. News is coming out that Nepal's national flag was not used during formal talks when our country's Honorable Finance Minister visited India. In bilateral talks between two friendly nations, the national flags of both countries should be present. However, the absence of Nepal's national flag is a serious violation of diplomatic dignity. What is the real fact of this incident? I demand that the government immediately clarify this incident. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota.
Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Honorable Chairperson, due to the war in the Middle East, Nepal is already facing an energy crisis. Although I have repeatedly spoken about energy, the current gas shortage is forcing everyone to pay around 3,000 rupees for a cylinder that costs 2,000. Currently, there are about 60 gas refilling industries in the country, each with cylinders labeled with their own names. They do not allow refilling of cylinders labeled with another company's name or their depots. Even if they do, they charge between 300 to 900 rupees. I have repeatedly requested the state to manage this and create a system for exchanging cylinders without charge. The ministry has changed, and the new minister should do something. I request that this system be made easier. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Somnath Poudel.
Honorable Member Somnath Poudel (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Honorable Chairperson, Rastriya Swatantra Party, which promised to bring special programs for the upliftment and development of the Dalit community, received a landslide victory. I don't know what else that landslide swept away, but it seems to have swept away the budget for the Dalit community. The government led by the then Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli of the Communist Party of Nepal (UML) had allocated a budget of 500 million rupees for the promotion of traditional occupations of the Dalit community. As soon as the current government was formed, 400 million rupees were re-appropriated in Baishakh 2083. Out of the remaining 100 million rupees, only 35 million 17 thousand 556 rupees were received by beneficiaries, and the remaining approximately 65 million rupees were frozen. The target was for over 1600 entrepreneurs to benefit from this program, but only 150 people benefited. This government not only did not allocate a budget for the Dalit community itself but also snatched away the budget allocated by the previous government. I condemn this act and demand that the budget be managed to compensate for it. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable members, the Zero Hour speaking session concludes here. Honorable members, names have been submitted on a party basis to speak during the Special Time. I will now provide time to speak to the Honorable Member. First, Honorable Member Anand Prasad Dhungana, time 20 minutes. Following this, Honorable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima".
Honorable Member Anand Prasad Dhungana (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson, I would like to present some points regarding the current political situation during the special time. First of all, I offer condolences and tributes to the Nepali brothers and sisters who lost their lives in the Bhote Koshi flood. I also express my condolences to their families. Furthermore, when the Bhote Koshi flood occurred, if there was a real all-party meeting, the Prime Minister should have called it. The Prime Minister did not call it. However, the Prime Minister did not attend the meeting called by the chairman of the ruling party. What does this show? It shows that somewhere, there is an internal conflict between the government and the chairpersons of the ruling party. If there is an internal conflict, they need to resolve it, manage it, and sort it out. And the proposal that came in the first all-party meeting, regarding how to manage this flood and how all parties should participate, and the proposal to form a special all-party parliamentary committee, has not been formed yet. What does this show? It shows that what the government says, it does not do. What it does not do, it says it does. Therefore, I think this needs to be understood.
Therefore, the government still has a chance. Because yesterday too, an all-party meeting was called. In that all-party meeting, it was said that the committee would be formed quickly. But that committee has not been formed yet. What does this mean? I have said this before. We speak during Zero Hour. We speak during Special Time. We speak on every issue in Parliament as representatives of the people. If the government does not respond, does not give an answer, does not show its presence, then there is no meaning in speaking. There is no meaning in this Parliament convening. If we are the representatives of the people, it feels useless to us too. When we go to the villages, to the districts, when we sit with friends, with the villagers, they say to us at the tea shops, "You speak, brother, but the government doesn't respond to it." So, can you tell the government? Can you tell them? Therefore, I want to say that the government has not yet responded in the National Assembly regarding the incident in Bhote Koshi. What happened there? What has happened? The Prime Minister may have answered in the House of Representatives. But it is not enough for the Prime Minister to answer only in the House of Representatives. This is a bicameral parliament, the House of Representatives and the National Assembly. Therefore, I don't think this government understands this. It needs to be responsible in the National Assembly too, it needs to say something in the National Assembly, and my words need to reach through the National Assembly. But this government does not understand this responsibility.
Therefore, I want to say that this government does not manage the decisions of the all-party meetings, does not arrange them. This government says it will do everything, but does not complete it. If the government continues to work in such an irresponsible manner, you will not get respite by just recounting 35 years of stories and saying that nothing happened in 34 years. I want to say this clearly. If you want to talk about 35 years to the public, you will need a list of how, where, and how much development has occurred in these 35 years. We have already stated this list in this house many times, and you are also aware of it. Therefore, I don't think the government is being responsible in this way. Now, the cabinet has decided that the Prime Minister will go to Europe, but what is the preparation for that? Will the information be provided to the house or not? What has been discussed with our neighboring countries regarding this? How much have neighboring countries been informed? Regarding the glaciers that caused such great damage to Nepal, I think the damage is unprecedented. Damage has occurred before, earthquakes occurred in '90, earthquakes have occurred here too. There have been many floods and landslides before. People were worried that the Sunkoshi might burst, and it was not that they weren't. But all those things were managed somehow, and the public was reassured.
What is your government doing today? There is a saying, "Playing a flute before a buffalo, the buffalo remains..."

"We have spoken so much, we have discussed so much. If you at least go and speak at the United Nations, I don't think the problems here will be resolved. Therefore, the government must hold all-party meetings to prepare for what the government is preparing. Informing the parliament means informing the public. Informing the parliament is not about informing 4, 10, 20, or 50 honorable members. It is about informing the public, informing Nepalis. I understand that the government is not responsible for this. Another thing is that we have said we don't want relief. We want compensation. We are the Himalayas; the glaciers there are causing these situations. According to the information I received, it took less than 10 minutes for the water from where the glacier burst to reach the Mitre Pul. It came rushing down like that. Therefore, scientists are saying that such incidents can happen again. In this situation, what is the government doing to manage it? Information about these matters is not being provided to the public through the parliament, the National Assembly, or the House of Representatives. In other words, I don't think it is taking responsibility. Now, during this time of national unity, the nation must be united. I remember when the earthquake happened in 2072 BS, the leader of the opposition stood up and said that now there is no ruling party or opposition within this parliament; we are all united in this time of national grief. I don't feel that we are in that situation today, nor has it been said. We don't know. We, the honorable members of the National Assembly, do not know that the Prime Minister, or a minister, or the Home Minister, has said that such major incidents have occurred. Now, there was a shooting in Captaganj, and someone was shot and admitted to the hospital. We have been in this parliament for many days and have seen that when any incident occurs in the country, either the Prime Minister or the Home Minister would come and inform the parliament. Through that, the people of the country would understand. Today, such a major incident happened in Sunsari and Siraha. The entire Madhesh became insecure. Everyone understood what would happen, whether it would be a caste riot or something else. But it was managed. So, what happened in Captaganj now? According to the information I received, they came on a motorcycle and shot and left. Are there committees to monitor how such wrong people come, shoot, and leave? Has the government appointed them to monitor? I think we should get information about all these things. This is a two-thirds government, but it doesn't matter just to say it's a two-thirds government. It must be able to make decisions and move forward. I would also like to raise one or two social issues. We are the people of a poor country. We have a lot of poverty. Because we are poor, those who earn in the morning eat in the evening. They have to go out to earn again the next day. But here, foreigners earn and keep wealth, and we eat that. They have given two days of holiday, Saturday and Sunday. Why is that needed? One day of holiday was for rest. They should have kept one day of holiday. How much loss has Nepal incurred from this increased one-day holiday? Has anyone provided information about what has been done? Has anyone experienced it? Has anyone studied it? It has not reached the education curriculum. It is affecting health. Our friends from Madhesh come, get sick, and are brought by ambulance. Today is Saturday, today is Sunday, it's a holiday, and they are not admitted to the hospital. Where to go? They are told to go to a private hospital, but they are poor people, and their condition is bad. Therefore, I want to say that we do not need two days of holiday. There was one day of holiday for rest, one day of rest after working seven days, and then they would work with new energy. Therefore, by doing these two days, we are not Americans; this is not America, this is not Britain. In places like India, there are not two days. Why do we need it here? Our lifestyle, habits, food, and earnings are all like those of the people of a poor country. Therefore, it is very difficult to understand why the government gave these two days of holiday and for what reason. Another thing is that offices open at 9:00 AM. If offices open at 9:00 AM, men can manage. They are not responsible for the household. Women have responsibilities. They have to feed their children, dress them, send them to school, and then go to work. Now, suppose a female employee from Bhaktapur has to come to Singha Durbar; she has to leave at 7:30 AM. Then, what will she teach her child, what will she dress her child in, what will she feed her child? I don't think an extra hour makes a big difference by opening at 10:00 AM. I don't think opening the office an hour earlier makes a big difference. What does this mean is that female employees, you should leave now. I see on TV sometimes, I was watching this morning, a millionaire said, 'If both of us earn, the children will become neglected, the children will not study, the children will be ruined. We thought we were both working for the sake of culture, but if it's not happening, I've given it up.' And he said to me, 'This is the wife's earnings, my wife works, and I eat the wife's earnings.' 'But I have sacrificed, and my wife earns and feeds the children, isn't that a good thing?' he replied in the millionaire show. What this means is that if female employees are truly needed in Nepal, it's not enough to say I made four women ministers. Have you provided facilities to all women? Have you tried to bring everyone to their rightful place? That's what people want to see. This government has not done that. Because if the office opens at 10:00 AM instead of 9:00 AM, there is no problem, nothing will be ruined. Therefore, I want to mention that point as well. Similarly, the Law Minister said that this year, on Law Day, we will pass 166 laws. Which ones will be passed? Which laws do the Nepali people need now? They need the Civil Service Act. They need the Army and Police Act. They need the Education Act. Are these available? None of them are a priority. No law is a priority for you. Which law is it? I don't want to say that any law is unimportant from this platform. But what is it? Which law needs to be passed immediately, and which can be passed later? It seems this government has no idea. Therefore, I don't feel that this government is actively working towards the progress of this country and the strengthening of federalism with a microscopic view. Therefore, I want to say that when we do anything, even at home, when we do our own work, we first decide whether to get our daughter married or our son married, and then we do it. But this government has no idea which law to bring and which not to bring. In our villages in Madhesh, they say, 'One goat for the sacrifice,' and it's like that. Therefore, my point is that the government should think and bring what is needed. I don't understand if it has understood the need. Therefore, I want to say from this platform that the government should use a little wisdom, the government should think a little and bring everything, and if there is any difficulty in thinking, there are opposition parties here, experienced people, they should consult with the experienced people and then do it. We don't want to say, 'Leave now, leave tomorrow,' to the government that the Nepali people have given a two-thirds majority. Work well, but work in such a way that the people understand that it is working well, but that is not the case. What do people say now? In our districts, people say, 'We voted for the bell symbol, but now we have to remain silent.' Now look, why was Bharat Dahal arrested? What did he say? He spoke about the 'grey zone' issue, about leaks in 'grey zone' journalism, on Facebook. We also brought a law in the National Assembly to manage this Facebook, this social media. It might have been a bit hasty, that's a different matter. That's why you are sitting here today, you have become ministers. Therefore, my point is, don't use language like, 'What didn't work yesterday, I won't do today.' Today, the Nepali people have given you responsibility; tomorrow, they can give it to someone else. This update election, this democracy, is not about one person ruling forever. In a democracy, the person loved by the people comes, the person loved by the people rules, the people rule. Not individuals, the people rule. Therefore, understand all those things. Another thing, the Prime Minister has been called to the House of Representatives so many times, I don't know, he says whatever he wants. Before speaking, consult with your own colleagues, we are not saying consult with us, but at least sit with your own colleagues and discuss whether this is appropriate to say, whether to say this or not. I don't see that happening either. Therefore, what is it, this government is like a government that says 'cars are coming and going.' Therefore, I don't feel that it has taken honesty and responsibility towards the Nepali people. Therefore, these three or four laws must come. Now I am hearing that the house will be closed on the 16th. Now, before the 16th, the Civil Service Act is not coming, the Education Act is not coming, the Police Act is not coming, none of them are coming. And employees will be 55 and 30. Why was it 60 before? It became 58, why was it 30, it remained 30, this needs to be studied. We have known from the beginning how 58 became 60. Now why is it being made 60? Previously, people's lifespan was not more than 60-65. Today, people's lifespan is not less than 71. It is assumed in our country that people live up to 71 years. Therefore, I want to say, therefore, we passed laws in the National Assembly and the House of Representatives with 60 and 30. We made 58 into 60. Now I hear that 54 employees will be removed, and 7,000 employees will be removed. And will the people you appoint all be your own people? Were the people we appointed all ours yesterday? No. They were people of the Nepali public. They were citizens of Nepal, and they were appointed. Have you removed those people through the ordinance you just issued, and have you brought in new people in the way you said you would? No, you haven't been able to do that.

Sir. So, what happens is, in the world, when anyone engages in politics, what has to happen is that one does not always remain. The king had that pride, the king was finished. Whoever had pride, all of them were finished. Therefore, we have a saying - 'Excessive pride leads to downfall, excessive ego leads to the Kauravas. Excessive charity leads to Bali being bound, everything in excess should be avoided.' Excess never lasts. Therefore, let us understand this and let the government work in that manner. Regarding the discussion on federalism at the present time, although I don't think you are in favor of federalism, because your party did not participate in federalism yesterday either. Even now, in your session, the Finance Minister brought a proposal to abolish federalism. Whether you could pass it is a different matter. The only reason you could not pass it is the pressure from the public. The public thought, 'If I pass this now, what will be my situation tomorrow?' For that reason, you did not pass it. Otherwise, if you had understood this, if you had understood that there are no elections in the near future, you would have passed it. Therefore, what I want to say is that let the government think now, it is not our wish for the government to step down, but if it is our wish for the government to step down, do you have a majority in the National Assembly? No, you don't. But we have passed it. You said that it should be passed in both houses, and that we do not have a majority in the upper house. But you have a majority, whatever you wanted has been passed here. Therefore, what I want to say is that at the present time, let this government proceed with restraint and order, that is our best wish. But if it continues to do wrong, just as any dictator who came was finished, may this government not meet the same fate, for that I have presented my views here. Thank you, Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima", time 14 (13:50 hrs) minutes. After this, Honorable Member Meena Singh Rakhal. Honorable Mr. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Communist Party of Nepal):- Honorable Chairperson, today I want to draw the special attention of the government through this respected house to a very important issue. With the main slogan 'Restoration of Trust, Management of Transformation, United Nations working for all', the 81st General Assembly of the United Nations has begun from September 8th. This General Assembly is an important opportunity for Nepal to clearly present its national interests and international issues to the global community. The head of government is going to participate in this occasion. We have received information that the Honorable Prime Minister will address the high-level session of the General Assembly from September 22 to 28. I express my heartfelt best wishes for the success of the Honorable Prime Minister's high-level visit and address on behalf of myself and my party, the Communist Party of Nepal. On this important occasion, I urge the Prime Minister to strongly raise issues of climate justice, loss and damage, and the Bhote Koshi flood in Rasuwa on behalf of Nepal to the global community, and I express my belief that he will succeed in drawing the world's attention through a strong presence. Honorable Chairperson, the visit and address of the Honorable Prime Minister are taking place at a time when Nepal is in mourning. It is suffering the punishment for mistakes it has not made. Yes, on Bhadra 10th, the Bhote Koshi brought devastation for us. Such devastation, which claimed thousands of lives, rendered many homeless, took away many supports, and ended many lineages. Today, some are searching for their family members, some are searching for their homes, some are searching for their livelihoods, children are searching for the warm embrace of their mothers and the shelter of their fathers. They are searching for drowned dreams and futures in the flood. The devastating flood of the Bhote Koshi destroyed property worth billions, pushed the country back 20 years, and gave a warning: if you want life on Earth, do not exploit nature, do not just take from nature, but also give to it. Honorable Chairperson, excessive exploitation of nature leads to destruction. It is necessary for people in the world to understand that human-made physical development for human comfort and happiness is not the only real development; it can also be destruction. If nature is tampered with too much, nature can become ferocious, and this is what happened in the Bhote Koshi of Rasuwa. Honorable Chairperson, Nepal's contribution to global greenhouse gas emissions is very low, but Nepal is bearing its impact disproportionately. We are forced to face risks such as melting glaciers, bursting glacial lakes, floods, landslides, droughts, and excessive rainfall, and these challenges are increasing. The Bhote Koshi flood has once again shown the seriousness of climate risks, and those who have contributed the least to creating the climate crisis are paying the highest price. This is climate injustice. The flood in the Bhote Koshi of Rasuwa cannot be seen merely as a natural disaster. Developed countries, which are the cause of greenhouse gas emissions, may try to blame nature to escape their responsibility for the damage caused by their earthquakes. Those days may also come. Such false facts must be refuted with diplomatic skill. This must be made a serious international issue, and that issue is climate justice. That issue is climate diplomacy. Honorable Chairperson, while saying this, has Nepal not raised the issue of climate justice in the world forum before? Nepal has continuously raised the issue of climate change and climate justice in international forums. In 1992, Nepal signed the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and ratified it in 1994. Since then, Nepal has been continuously raising its voice as a country with low emissions but bearing the unequal impact of climate change. It has not only raised its voice but is also fulfilling its responsibility to prevent global temperature rise. I want to recall today, as institutional memory, Nepal's decades-long policies, diplomatic initiatives, contribution to Himalayan conservation, and demands for climate justice, and I urge the government to move forward based on institutional memory. Honorable Chairperson, Nepal's history of raising the issue of climate change is long. It can be said that since the beginning of the international climate journey, Nepal has been at the forefront, struggling for climate justice for developing countries. Nepal has been participating in the annual climate conferences under UNFCCC, known as 'COP', since the beginning and raising climate issues. There is a history of the then Ambassador to Belgium, Durgesh Man Singh, participating as Nepal's representative in the first COP in 1995. Since then, Heads of State and Heads of Government have given importance to this and have presented Nepal's position on climate change in various COPs. In COP15 held in Copenhagen in 2009, then Prime Minister Madhav Kumar Nepal, in COP20 in 2014, then Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli, in COP26 and COP27 held in 2020 and 2022, then Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba, in CP28 in 2023, then Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal 'Prachanda', in C0P24 in 2018, then President Bidya Devi Bhandari, and in CP in 2024, President Ram Chandra Paudel participated. All of them not only raised the issue that Nepal's contribution to climate change is negligible but it is bearing significant damage, but they also strongly raised the issue of environmental protection being linked to human existence. Similarly, Nepal has been strongly raising the issue of climate in the General Assembly of the United Nations. In the 61st General Assembly of the United Nations in 2006, then Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister KP Sharma Oli spoke about climate change and its impact on Nepal. In the 63rd and 71st General Assemblies, then Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal 'Prachanda' said, 'Saving the Himalayas is not just saving the Himalayas, but saving humanity.' In the 71st General Assembly, he committed to reducing carbon emissions to zero by 2045 and strongly demanded compensation for the impact Nepal has suffered due to excessive greenhouse gas emissions from developed countries, in return for its role in environmental protection. Not only that, he invited the then Secretary-General of the United Nations, Ban Ki-moon, to Nepal. Although the main objective was peace, he took him on a helicopter tour of the Himalayas to show the reality of how climate change is affecting the Himalayas. In the 64th General Assembly, then Prime Minister Madhav Kumar Nepal, in the 66th General Assembly, then Prime Minister Baburam Bhattarai, in the 67th General Assembly, then Head of Government Khilraj Regmi, and in the 72nd General Assembly, then Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba strongly presented Nepal's position regarding the Himalayas, environmental protection, sustainable development, and responsibility. Honorable Chairperson, the former Prime Minister Madhav Kumar Nepal has made an unforgettable and important contribution to Nepal's climate diplomacy. When he was Prime Minister, on Mangsir 19, 2066 BS, or December 4, 2009, he held a cabinet meeting at the world's highest peak, Sagarmatha Base Camp, Kalapatthar. This location is at an altitude of 5,542 meters above sea level. This was a milestone in Nepal's climate diplomacy history. This meeting took place one week before COP 15 held in Copenhagen, Denmark. The purpose of holding the cabinet meeting at Kalapatthar was to draw the world's attention to the impact of climate change in the Himalayan region. Nepal has the world's largest ice reserves. The source of water for 10 major river systems in Asia is in Nepal, and the water supply for about 2 billion people is in Nepal, and the message was that this source is depleting. The meeting pledged to mitigate the effects of climate change and issued a 10-point Sagarmatha Declaration. This meeting decided to establish the Api Nampa Conservation Area in Darchula, the Gaurishankar Conservation Area in Ramechhap and Dolakha, and the Banke National Park. Through the Kalapatthar meeting, Nepal succeeded in alerting the world to climate change in a very sensitive and strong manner. Not only that, but by bringing a stone from Kalapatthar to COP15, he symbolically presented it to the then US President Barack Obama with the main message that due to the excessive greenhouse gas emissions of developed countries like yours, our Himalayas are melting, and the white Himalayas are turning black. That stone is still in the office of the US President as a gift. That was Nepal's climate diplomacy. In 2024, the government organized the Sagarmatha Dialogue in Kathmandu to raise climate issues. Similarly, from the private sector, the Himalayan Climate Charter was organized in Namche, Solukhumbu on June 1, 2026. This program was organized by SPCC. Honorable Sonam Geljen Sherpa, Honorable Madan Kumari Shah "Garima", Honorable Aakriti Awasthi, Honorable Krantishikha Dhital, Honorable Kamal Subedi, and former Speaker Shivamaya Tumbahamphe participated in this program and expressed their commitment to environmental protection. Honorable Chairperson, looking at Nepal's journey in climate diplomacy, one thing is clear. Since signing the UNFCCC in 1992, Nepal has been raising issues of equality, common but differentiated responsibilities, and financial and technical assistance. Later, the special risks of the Himalayas, climate

Loss and damage, such as justice, climate adaptation, and compensation, have been added to Nepal's international priorities. Therefore, the flood in Bhote Koshi, Rasuwa, must be viewed in conjunction with this long diplomatic journey, and compensation must be demanded accordingly. Scientific records of flood damage must be presented to strengthen the demand for compensation. Nepal's demand should not be limited to the emotional appeal of 'Save the Himalayas.' International cooperation is essential for climate finance, technology transfer, research, early warning systems, and damage and risk assessment for Himalayan countries, and the Honorable Prime Minister will raise this voice forcefully in that forum.

Honorable President, I would like to draw your attention in the end and express my best wishes for the success of the visit, and I also want to express my belief that Nepal will be successful in obtaining compensation for the irreparable damage it has suffered due to developed nations, and I also wish good luck. Thank you.

President, today I want to draw the government's attention to a very serious political, social, and economic issue. Cooking gas is not a luxury item. It is a necessary and consumable item for ordinary citizens. But today, citizens have to stand in line for hours, carry empty cylinders to depots, and in some places, pay more than the fixed price. Mr. President, according to available data, while the daily requirement in the Kathmandu Valley is around 35 to 40 thousand cylinders, it is reported that in the recent crisis, the demand has reached about 1 lakh cylinders per day. On September 8, it was reported that only nine dealers in the valley received supplies. Although the price set by the government is around 2,165, consumers in some places have had to pay 2,500 to 3,000.

Mr. President, it is true that the supply system has faced serious problems due to floods, landslides, and road blockages in Krishnabhir. However, natural disasters cannot be used as an excuse to neglect black marketing, artificial shortages, unequal distribution, and weaknesses in market monitoring. The important aspect is that due to the interdependent relationship between humans and animals, this bill identifies, combats, prevents, controls, and eradicates infectious diseases in animals, and provides the necessary legal provisions for animal health, public health, and production. Therefore, the proposed form is a very important aspect. During the extensive discussions within this, three or four important issues were raised, and the Honourable Minister's very simple, easy-going nature and coordination played a role. He easily accepted the proposals we made in the amendments. Laws are not made for the sake of making them; they are made for the public, for the farmers, and 3-4 issues have been included in this, which is a matter of pride. Number 1 is that the definition of epidemic and infectious disease has been made, which was very important. Similarly, there is a new provision for compensation, relief fund, and relief benefits. Generally, the Ministry of Finance does not approve this. It is a difficult situation. Despite that, because the Government of Nepal and the Minister have been very positive with us, we have succeeded in including this. Similarly, insurance arrangements have been made. Now, I would only like to request that all colleagues in the Legislation Committee and all Members of Parliament be informed that this has reached a conclusion from all stakeholders. While all are deserving of thanks, the implementation aspect should also be given special attention by the Government of Nepal, as the law alone is not enough. I request this and also request that this be passed unanimously by our Legislation Committee. Thank you. Jai Nepal. Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Ms. Ram Kumari Jhankri. Honourable Ms. Ram Khumari Jhankri (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honourable Chairperson, the Honourable Members who spoke before have already highlighted the main points of the discussion on the report of the Infectious Animal Disease (Control) Bill, 2083. We have all put in some effort. When making laws, they should be idealistic and implementable. The government and parliamentarians have made equal efforts. When we discussed at the level of experts, they also told us the same thing, so it seems we have worked diligently on this bill. In doing so, we have done remarkable work, especially in the areas of epidemics, their control, responsibility, disease control, and relief and compensation. As a result, when animals die due to epidemics or infectious diseases, and farmers are distressed, the fund for long-term relief, compensation, and rehabilitation is a remarkable achievement. How this fund will be managed will be determined by the regulations later. However, we have also discussed some matters. We believe the government will work without undermining the main spirit. This is because if annual budget-approved programs are brought for compensation, and if there is no epidemic or infectious disease in that year, the budget will be frozen annually. For this reason, when the ministry presents the approved program, if the government brings this fund, it will be utilized and not frozen, and this fund will grow, and the government, the Ministry of Agriculture, will be able to provide rehabilitation when farmers face hardship, which is our belief. Therefore, it has been managed by the ministry and the department with their own team rather than by outsiders. In doing so, it is implementable, and even then, there were some minor lapses. We realized later that some representatives of the ministry were missed in the response committee in the House of Representatives. We believe the Honourable Minister will correct this in the House of Representatives, and we have tried to make a good law. (Time expired.) Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma. Honourable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Nepal Communist Party):- Honourable (14:02 PM)

Mr. Speaker, today we are discussing the bill related to Infectious Animal Diseases (Control) Bill, 2083, along with the report of the Legislation Management Committee, and we are currently on the motion to pass it. First and foremost, I would like to thank our honorable Minister. There were some shortcomings in this bill, so we had submitted amendments. Following discussions with the ministry, experts, the Minister's own arguments, and the debates and arguments of us, the amendment proposers and committee members, the Minister supported them. We also found the Minister's arguments to be good. Therefore, this report has come with full consensus, and we have discussed the bill in the committee. Thus, first of all, I want to thank the Minister. Specifically, the preamble seemed a bit confusing, which we have comprehensively improved. There also seemed to be some issues with the definition of epidemic and epidemic-related animal diseases. We have also improved and further enriched this through extensive discussion. Thus, on one hand, for the control of animal diseases, we have also made arrangements to utilize private organizations established according to prevailing laws. On the other hand, there was no fund for compensation and relief. Therefore, our discussion demanded the need for such a fund, and that fund has been established. A Compensation and Relief Fund has been established. Thus, that relief fund, compensation fund was essential. We had to provide compensation. Thus, a fund was needed to fulfill the need for relief, and we have made arrangements for that fund. Furthermore, by adding sub-section 2 after sub-section 1 of Section 29, we have made provisions to give priority to economically disadvantaged, poor, helpless, single women, marginalized classes, and communities when providing compensation and relief. Thus, I believe it has become more enriched, beautiful, and refined. Therefore, I support this bill along with the report and also request that it be passed. Thank you.
